title: Is 8 Allowed? Linear Inequalities Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
A lift sign says maximum eight persons. Eight people is fine, nine sets off the alarm, yet the sign never uses an equals sign. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 5, Linear Inequalities) we meet the maths behind it: the inequality.

You will see a balance scale tip, learn the four symbols <, >, ≤ and ≥ with the open mouth rule, and watch a live test run every value of p through p ≤ 8 on a number line, then lose one answer when the little line is removed. We compare strict and slack inequalities (empty and filled circles), name the NCERT kinds (numerical, literal, double, linear), and see why an equation has one answer but an inequality has a whole stretch. Two pause-and-think questions, the NCERT rice packets example, the exam trap about "not more than", an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.

In this video:

2:47 One answer vs a whole stretch
3:15 Worked example: rice packets (NCERT)
3:54 Exam trap: not more than
4:22 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
4:59 Recap and three questions to answer
